utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Pilipovic, you are ready to resume the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it please you, Mr. President, if for a moment I could just bring to the attention of the Court the fact that the witness, Richard Philipps, is still waiting and available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So, I am not sure and I don't expect that the witness presently being taken will be all day, all three sessions today. However, I did raise it with my friends yesterday an apparently they will have problems with that. So perhaps if we would determine what we are going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic, what would be a problem if we would continue with Mr. Philipps?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday the Defence and the Chamber received a schedule for the following week and we can see that from the schedule, Mr. Philipps was suggested to appear on Tuesday, that is for the 16th of July. The information that Philipps would be heard the following day, that is today, was told to us by the learned colleague yesterday. But we wanted to find out, Mr. Piletta-Zanin and I, wanted to know what we would be doing today. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we wanted to know whether we would have a full working day today and I wanted to know about the scheduled today. And then yesterday it was 1900 hours I was told that my learned colleagues had intention of continuing to hear Mr. Philipps. I would just like to draw the attention of the Chamber, that according to the schedule, we had Mr. Philipps last Friday and on Monday. And bearing in mind the decision -- because of the decision of the Chamber, there was also our expert who was present on Friday and Monday. But since the decision regarding his stay was until Tuesday, he had to return, and leave The Hague because his authorisation was only for five working days. So we thought, our assessment was that he had to return, because that is what the rules were. We couldn't ask for him to stay any longer because we wouldn't -- we did not know that our learned friends had intended to hear Mr. Philipps today. If they had told us that earlier, then we would have found an opportunity for our expert to remain here and to hear Mr. Philipps. But as I am telling you, we only heard that last night. Mr. Radinovic was here for five working days and I don't think it is not really seemly to spend so much money and without the expert being here. We believe that if Mr. Philipps is going to be heard today, then I believe that this would not be good for the Defence. I don't understand. We have a right to have our expert to be present, Mr. Radinovic, I don't understand why we were told this at such a -- such a belated time. I don't think that we can accept that Mr. Philipps be heard today, particularly since we have -- did ask the Prosecution whether Mr. Philipps would be heard on Tuesday, in order not to have Mr. Radinovic be here for longer than necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, would you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am afraid that I am not in a position to be accurate as to the history of what was said or what was not said exactly. However, if the Defence expert has had to leave because of visa limitations, I do confess that I am sympathetic to the position of the Defence. However, I wonder whether or not if they would be biased or any way in prejudice was just taken in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just taken in achievement, may I ask, Ms. Pilipovic, whether it would help if you would take the tape with the B/C/S translation to the expert so he can, although not officially, but orally could follow every detail that he heard here and see whether that would be a presence, a distance, more or less, so that you are able to prepare for cross-examination, even after today so that we would start with chief. Would that be an acceptable solution for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if there is a possibility for us to receive a tape immediately after the examination today, then the Defence would accept this solution in order not to waste time. But we just wanted our colleagues to confirm that Mr. Philipps' examination would continue on Tuesday so that we have -- so that we know that when Mr. Radinovic comes he doesn't have to wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then, of course, we would have to know exactly how we then proceed, because it is very unfortunate, we said that already Monday in the afternoon that we would not continue with Mr. Philipps. And of course, the Defence could not properly prepare when the examination-in-chief is not yet over and when the expert could not have heard the evidence given by Mr. Philipps. Perhaps we will have a short break when we finish with the present witness and then, first of all, find out whether it would be possible for you to get a tape of the B/C/S translation of what Mr. Philipps will say. Then at the same time, that the Prosecution informs us about when Mr. Philipps would be called to be cross-examined. Would that be a provisional solution? So we will --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can say that if Mr. Philipps is going to be scheduled for Tuesday, and if the learned colleagues can confirm that he will appear on Tuesday, then we would be prepared for Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My last schedule of today is the 15th, that is next Monday, isn't it? Mr. Philipps is scheduled for the 16th, as far as I can see on my update I just received. So the main risk would be about the witness scheduled on Monday. You say it is four hours. Would that include cross-examination? If you are not quite sure, Mr. Stamp, perhaps you better find out and then inform the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we could deal with it after this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's first then start and, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Dr. Kovacs. Dr. Kovacs, may I -- may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good Kovacs, good morning.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, in your report on page 9 --

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, I haven't got a copy of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, on page 9, it starts on page 8 and then it continues on page 9 -- in your report, when you were discussing the destruction of targets, you said that in case that targets, uncovered targets --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So in your report, page 9, I am interpreting your words, I am paraphrasing you spoke of about "unobservable targets" and you said, "if a target is not observable and 120 millimetre mortar is used to fire at it at a distance of 4 kilometres, and an open target is being fired at, it is necessary to fire 80 to 100 shells in order to destroy the target." Did I understand this correctly?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes you did. However I have to add that this was just an example and basically does not include all the necessary data which I obviously did not possess. So this is just an approximate example. I just wanted to show you the differences in dimensions, when firing at open and covered targets. And I wanted to demonstrate the magnitude of destruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But you did establish that it was necessary to fire between 80 and 100 shells in order to destroy the target?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is true. But I would like to emphasise that this is just an example, chosen at random among the artillery weapons, which I choose and that I chose the firing distance and all the other conditions of firing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, could you tell us what is the probability to hit such a target with only one shell?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean to say whether it is probable to hit a target with one single fire or shooting?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I am in a position to give you a satisfactory answer to that question because there are so many things that should be taken into consideration. And there are so many other factors which might be considered as a risk. Therefore, it is not possible to give a satisfactory answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, from your experience, do you know if an unobservable target at a distance of 2000 metres can be fired at with only one mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 200 or 2000 metres?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday we spoke about the fact that when it comes to non-observable targets firing involves different conditions and circumstances than in the case of observable targets. Taking into consideration all this, I think that when it comes to a non-observable target, the probability of hitting a target like that, with one shell only, is very little.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, on page 9 paragraph 2, we can call it 2A, you spoke about the destruction of live troops, live forces, and if I understood you correctly, you said that it is necessary to use ammunition with smallest possible charge because that is how the firing can be done with a specific angle.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where this is in the text because I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, it is called a live forces and weapons located in the open or under cover. The following sentence is that the firing must be carried out with the smallest possible charge as this allows a greater firing angle and therefore a correspondingly greater striking angle. And you said that this ensures the greatest fragmentation effect. In accordance with what you stated here, can you tell us, what would be the charge in a shell, in a mortar shell of 120 millimetres, what would be the charge that would allow for the greatest effect in destroying live troops or live forces?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In case of mortars and mortar shells, the ignition charge can be changed and as I said, this depends on the firing distance and this is very important. The smallest possible charge is supposed to be used and this is done this way because in that case the striking angle is going to be bigger at the target as well. And if the striking angle is greater, the fragmentation effect of the shell will be bigger after the detonation. And this is true because fragments coming from the body of the shell or the whole of the shell, will be absorbed by the ground in fewer numbers. Because all this depends on the striking angle of the shell. The bigger the striking angle, the fewer fragments will be absorbed. So to sum it up, we can achieve the greatest possible striking angle when using a mortar, if we use the smallest possible charge, depending on the firing distance in the mortar. As regards to the quantity of this charge, we have to use the quantities that can be found in the artillery table. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, could you tell us what would that smallest possible charge be?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The smallest possible charge always depends on the firing distance. You have to choose the smallest possible charge so that it can cover this firing distance in question, but at the same time, provide the greatest possible striking angle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, is that -- Mr. Kovacs, in your opinion, is this smallest possible charge of a shell the basic charge of the shell?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I am not in a position to give you an exact answer here because I don't know the firing distance and I don't know the data on the artillery table either. The smallest possible charge can be the basic charge, but it can be more than that as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, on page 11 paragraph 5, you spoke of the artillery positions on mountains. So that is part of the subsection, the application of artillery in combat against cities and paragraph 5 beginnings: "It is a particular case if the mountain surrounding the city around the side of the one of the parties for then this party can see every part of the city." You said that even a projectile, the strike of projectiles can be observed from the mortar firing posts. Now my question is whether from such positions that you cited here, it is possible to see the location where the shell lands, if that position or that location is between a high-rise buildings?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again, the basic question is if the target is observable or not. If the target is observable, obviously you can observe the effect of the fire as well. It is another question whether we are talking about a special situation in which from the firing post, that is the mortar firing post in our case, we can see the target and we can see the effect of the fire as well. This can make particularly accurate of the actual firing. It can facilitate and speed up firing as well. If the target is situated among tall buildings, the key issue is, again, whether from this firing post or another observation post, this particular target can be observed or not and, therefore, the effect of the fire can be observed or not. If this is so, whatever I described in my document is to -- for an answer to your question as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, on page 12 of your report, you speak about the optimal conditions which can improve the accuracy. It is line 6 from the top of the page. You speak about accuracy. And then you say what are the crucial requirements to reduce to a minimum the number of civilian casualties. And under G, and that would be the last item, the last dash in your list --

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the last paragraph, because I don't have a letter sign at the paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's right, Mr. Kovacs. You say that accuracy also requires that the first hit of the ranging fire be directed at a location where civilian casualties are not probable, where it is probable that there will be no civilian casualties. So, when you speak about this method with regard to accuracy, you speak about an endeavour to direct the first hit of the ranging fire to a location where it is probable there will be no civilian casualties. Tell us in a centre of a city, can one find a location at which to fire a ranging shot without consequence?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand your question. According to me, the following facts should be taken into account: My description indicates an existing firing situation. This procedure is employed if friendly troops or any other troops or civilians would be endangered. In this case, the elements of the first firing should be calculated in such a way that the shell should hit an area that can be well observed, at the same time, is farther away from the incriminated area. This is because after this the corrected fire, the second shot of the corrected fire, will most probably be closer to the target. Concerning the second part of your question, I would like to reply: In a city, I would like to stress this is not a concrete city, I could imagine an area with no problem that would meet these demands, and according to me, even with this firing you have to be cautious. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, would you say that it is permissible that the troops, military equipment, weapons, be deployed in areas where there are civilians? Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you specify your question? If I am on one side, do you mean the soldiers and civilians of the other side?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, let us try to imagine a part of a city and say that it is inhabited by civilians. Then, according to you, is it permissible that in that part of the city or in one building which is inhabited by civilians, is it allowed to have military equipment, a military unit, that is, a military facility there?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Now the question is clear to me. I feel that your question is rather addressing legal and moral issues, than artillery expertise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacs. Mr. Kovacs, on page 13 of your report in paragraph 3, you say that when the destruction of military objects is the real aim, the use of artillery, when larger number of civilian casualties are to be expected, is terrorism. Can you tell us, what is terrorism according to you?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exactly find where this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We all have difficulties in finding the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 30. So it is the last part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the problem, is in the transcript it reads "13." And therefore, we are looking at the wrong page. So it is the last page of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, paragraph three.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found the sentence you are addressing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, are you telling us that the use of artillery in any city is terrorism, to your mind?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I am claiming. I have a more nuanced opinion. I think, as I mentioned before, in any case, in any such target, when you demolish such a target where civilian casualties may occur, the commander has to weigh all factors so that the result that you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hope to achieve is in proportion with the civilian losses. In this area, I feel, as I described in the sentence, if the commander of that level issues a command within a battle in a city where artillery is used and it is known that many civilian casualties may occur, then what I described is valid. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacs, are you telling us that the bombing of Hiroshima, Nagasaki, Belgrade, is terrorism, too, according to you.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question you are asking is transgressing the limit of my expertise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. The Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Stamp, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said yesterday in answer to my learned friend that a brigade artillery group would be -- would normally be under the command of a corps commander and you also answered some question in respect to units and subunits. Could you just clarify what you understand to be a brigade artillery group?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I will explain. In the course of yesterday, it became apparent when I was asked these questions that the different organisational units -- there are changes between -- in the differences and a concrete answer would only be possible if these organisational units are exactly limited. Yesterday, when we spoke about this, I felt that there was some confusion between the organisational units. I couldn't reply in an exact manner. If we are to talk about this, we should define the organisational unit that I am supposed to reply about. But I would like to point out that I am not familiar with the corps command level. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you could not answer satisfactory about whether it is possible to hit a target with a single fire because there are many factors that are taken into consideration. Could you elaborate a little bit these factors that you take into consideration?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I would like to explain. When firing shell, you are using an artillery weapon. This may be a mortar. There are many factors that determine the accuracy of the firing. Without being exhaustive, I would like to sum up a few. The measurement of the position of the firing location is determining. The exact determination of the coordinates of the target are decisive. The level of training of the handlers are decisive, is decisive. The technical state of the mortar is decisive. The type of mortar, the production year, the maintenance state of the mortar is decisive. The firing load. Other ballistic circumstances and I would like to give some examples of these. The direction and the force of the wind is very decisive, and other extreme meteorological circumstances. Apart from this, there is also the factor of uncertainty which we call the "scattering" of the shell. And it is also complex of factors and this we cannot influence in practice. I hope that in these few sentences, I have given you an impression how complex it is to determine the first firing or the circumstances around the first firing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, bearing -- sorry -- a reasonably well trained mortar or artillery crew, having regard to all the factors which effect artillery fire, and applying what you have called in your report, "the proper correction data," is it possible for them to hit a target first shot through what you have described as "transfer of fire"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question is composed of two parts. I feel that a good well trained crew, that is well familiar with the target area, will take into account all factors mentioned by me or not mentioned by me for correction. All of these will contribute to an improvement of the probability of hitting the target at first -- with first shell. But I cannot answer how much better the hitting rate will be at first firing. Regarding the second part of the question, concerning the firing at the target, I think that the target to be eliminated, in the surroundings of this target to -- go eliminated another target that has already been fired at from that mortar from that position, the correction factors for those previous targets are already known. This includes all correction factors I mentioned before. This will be taken into account by the commander of the given level. Then the accuracy of the first firing will be greatly increased. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What do you mean by "greatly increased"? Perhaps if I ask you this way, how far or near to the target is it possible for them to get in terms of metre?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned before, I cannot give you exact data. It is conceivable that the first shell will fall in the immediate vicinity of the target but it is also conceivable that in spite of all the correction measures taken, the shell will hit outside the targeted area. Experience i.e. mathematics tell us, and of course ballistics tell us, that taking into account all of the factors, of the relevant factors, should considerably increase the accuracy. But without having seen it, it is not possible to say. It is always decided by practice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In your city you mentioned that you have studied the history of artillery. Could you illustrate us with some examples of cities in the modern history of artillery, let's say after the Second World War, which have been besieged as Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir I understand the question. If we talk about the history of modern -- modern history of artillery, we could also include the pre-World War II period, for I have to add that the basic changes in technique of artillery did not change so much in the past decades as we might think. The conventional artillery also uses means today of which less modern, but similar versions, were used in the Second World War. These conventional firing equipment is the equipment that didn't bring much news in the past decades. I am referring to the conventional firing equipment that are described in the report. In the framework of my work I am mostly involved with the artillery in the Second World War and the First World War. As I said, the minor changes in this equipment is also continuing until this day. If I claim that in the siege of city during the Second World War the procedures used in artillery are similar to the methods in the middle of the 19th Century, I am not far beside the truth. The concrete question by Your Honour, I would like to answer that similar cases during the Second World War were numerous. I could mention a similar case in my country the siege of the capital Budapest. During the siege, enormous amounts of artillery were used by the Soviet troops. The losses caused by Russian artillery were enormous. It is difficult to separate the military targets and civilian areas, but this siege, too, as many other sieges, had civilian casualties. I think, however, that the Second World War, during the Second World War similar events happened in the siege of other cities as well. So there are historical examples that are similar to the means of destruction and procedures used in the 80s and 90s. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. The fire of a tank is considered direct or indirect fire?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the contemporary versions of tanks are suitable for both types of firing. Basically I have to say that direct firing is their main objective, but the -- tanks are also suitable for indirect fire. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: What do you call "contemporary versions"?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am referring to those versions that were built in the 60s 70s 80s, and later in the military industry of the east or the west. In my own army, I could mention some types we use there. T-54, T-55, T-72, T-55 AM. This is a Hungarian version. All of these are suitable for direct or indirect firing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Which is the maximum range of a mortar, let's say, 120 millimetres mortar, maximum range?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: 120 millimetre mortar would have a maximum range that depends on the exact type of mortar. It also depends on the type of ammunition used. I could give you an indication. With conventional ammunition, 120 millimetre mortar would have a maximum range of about 6.000 metres. There may be deviations with regard to the ammunition used. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, I have a preliminary question for you. Do mortar shells always have tail-fins, stabilisers?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in conventional shells, mortar shells that I also mentioned in the course of today, that would be tail-fins at any case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the use for -- of tail-fins, what they do is in a way to adjust the firing, in some way?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not really what matters. The tail-fins found on mortar shells, they have a primary function to stabilise them in their trajectory. If this would not be the case, the shell would follow an irregular course and it would be impossible for the guidance -- for the guiding person to control it. So the role of the tail-fin of the mortar shell is to stabilise the fired shell in its trajectory. When the shell hits the target, it has no role at all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My following question would be: In your opinion, in order to determine where a round has come from, where a shell was fired from, when we look at the crater and the position of the stabiliser, is the position of the stabiliser of the tail-fin in the way that it is placed in a crater, is this something that we can rely upon in order to determine where the shell was fired from?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will try to given an answer as complete as possible to your question, taking into account that my training does not include to analyse shell craters. But based on my experiences in artillery, I can say that the form, the shape of the shell crater, the depth, and possibly the situation of the tail-fin of the shell after detonation may indicate the origins from where the shell was fired. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you as well, Mr. Kovacs. May I first take you back to yesterday where questions were put to you in respect of the sound. Distinction was then made between the firing sound and the sound of the impact. One question put to you was about the sound of a mortar shell during its trajectory. So after firing and before impact. You said: "You've got to note that the speed on the ammunition of the trajectory is that you can't really see it." The question was about hearing and you continued: "There is a sound effect on the basis of which an ordinary lay person or an expert could not specify 100 per cent what kind of shell it was. Because of the high speed of these shells, they are invisible on the trajectory." Since the question was about the sound of a shell during its trajectory, did I understand your answer well that you could hear a shell on its trajectory, but that you could not, by that sound, identify specifically what shell it would be, or did I misunderstand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I try to go into details about the question that you have just asked. There are three types of sound effects, I think. The first sound is when the shell is actually fired. When the shell leaved the barrel of the mortar, this is a sound which can be heard from miles away from several kilometres away because it has got a very characteristic sound. The second sound we have mentioned in connection with the trajectory. Here I said that the sound can only be heard on the trajectory when we are close to the trajectory, when we are close to the impact site or when we are close to the third location, that is, where the shell is actually fired from. And this is likely when we are talking about artillery, cannons, that is the fact that this sound is something that you can actually hear. The sound on the trajectory of the shell can only be heard when I am in the vicinity of that particular trajectory. And for instance, the shell is passing above my head or near me on its trajectory. The third sound that we have mentioned is the sound --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was mainly interested in this second type of sound. If you say if the shell is flying over your head in its trajectory, would a normal civilian, so not a specifically trained person, be able to discern this sound from other sounds? I mean would it be such that a normal not specifically trained civilian could identify that as a sound of a projectile? And what would that sound approximately be?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I understand your question. And what I would say is that an ordinary lay person will not be able to identify the shell on the basis of the sounds that particular person can hear. When I was talking about eyewitnesses of people who could actually hear certain sounds, can distinguish various impact sounds, I meant the third type of sound, which is the sound of the impact of the shell at the target. Because that sound has very special characteristics. I think that those who can hear or see things like that for the first or the second time, can give you an approximate account of such phenomenon and this might be the basis for you to have an idea. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I bring you back to the second sound. A shell flying over my head. So I do understand that a lay person could hear it. What would you expect a lay person to describe if he would have heard a shell flying over his head?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, now, coming back to the second type of sound. I think that if you take artillery weapons and here I don't principally mean mortars, but, first of all, I would like to mention cannons and the other type of very important weapons which is Howitzers, I think it is very important to distinguish between the shells of such weapons because the speed at which shells fly is completely different, and the trajectories are different as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we would take as an example a 120 millimetre mortar flying over my head, and I would have to describe to you what I heard and let's assume that the trajectory was not very flat, not very steep, something in between, what would you expect me, as a layman, to describe if I would describe the sound I hear?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that the sound a lay person would hear in that case, although I don't think it very probable for a mortar shell to be heard actually because its trajectory is very steep, and it can have a sound which can be heard at the particular instances or parts of its trajectory, that is, close to the target and close to the post where it was fired from. But if that person can hear the sound, I do not think that he or she would be able to distinguish between the sounds. Because one must have heard quite a few times the sound of shells to be able to do that, and to have an idea of what kind of sound he or she has just heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that to make that distinction that you need to have heard more shells. But given the example, would you expect someone to say it was a low sizzling sound or no, it was a high "bits". What would you expect the person to tell you.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, artillery mortar shells on their trajectories will have a kind of whistling sound, if you can hear them at all, while they are kind of advancing in the air. Obviously talking about artillery shells, this sound is much stronger because the shell is actually turning around on its trajectory. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand that a stabiliser fin prevents it from turning or does it make it turn?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually the role of a stabiliser fin is not to make it turn, basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, you would say that if there is a stabiliser fin, it would have the effect that the shell would not turn, not rotate, and, therefore, would make less sound than other projectiles?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I am saying is that if there were no tail-fins on the shells, the shells given their shape because they actually have the shape of a drop, would have a kind of bumping movement on their trajectories. This happens when the leading fin is damaged at the moment when the shell is fired or a small bit comes off it. In a case like that, it has got a typical sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for these answers. May I take you back to your report, page 16, and I would like to show you a document. Madam Registrar, could the witness be shown P2261. And could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. perhaps be placed on the ELMO the ERN, number ending with 4117 which is the 26th page of this 46-page document. Yes, that is the page. Could that please be placed on the ELMO. Dr. Kovacs, if this picture, and I am referring to the picture, not the small one under "A," but the big picture. If that would be the picture of the pattern of damage made by the impact of a mortar shell, and if someone would have told you that the angle of descent would have been 60 degrees would there be anything in this picture --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Excuse me, did you say ascent or descent?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Descent. Would be 60 degrees, would there be anything in this picture which would -- would contradict that conclusion? So I am not asking you whether this would a picture you would be able to establish that it was 60 degrees, but if someone would say that this is the picture of a 60-degree angle of descent impact of a mortar, would there be anything in this picture that would cause you to say, no, that could not have been a 60-degree angle of descent for such-and-such reason?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, you have also mentioned that there is not enough information at my disposal to give you a satisfactory answer to this question. Because this is just a drawing and I haven't done the analysis of the crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. You say the information given to me does not enable me to make whatever comment either positive or negative?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I could give you my own opinion, but I must point out that this is just my opinion and just at first sight and without any previous analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I am asking if you please give us your opinion and I take it that it is based upon your experience then.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously I have already seen quite a few of these. I have already seen quite a few craters. And on the basis of my experience, I think that since the crater, the shape of the crater is close to a circle, and if this shows us the direction of the spreading of the fragments, although I am not quite sure about that, and I am asking you, Your Honour, whether the bottom part of the drawing shows the damage caused by the fragments or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I understand, the picture reflects the damage on the surface caused by the impact of a mortar shell. So the pattern of the damage.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the back part of the effect of the shell does not give me sufficient background information, so I mean the top part of the drawing. But on the basis of what I can see, I think that -- and I have got to emphasise on the basis of what I can see now -- I think that it is very likely that the striking angle or the impact angle was more than 60 degrees. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us anything about how much more or would that not be possible? If you say, I can't do that -- we want reliable answers. So if you can do it reliably, please, and if you can't, please say you cannot.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that I wouldn't be able to give you a reliable answer. Therefore, I would rather not answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These were my questions, Dr. Kovacs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am wondering from that if I can just qualify one or two things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, related to the questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we have -- if it would just take two or three minutes, fine, otherwise we would first have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You referred to, from the translation, the turning of the artillery of the shell which are not mortar, in the air?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, we can't see the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now this spin on artillery, not being mortar shells, is it caused by the rifling of the barrel of the artillery gun?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are not talking about mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We are talking -- we are not talking about mortars. We are talking about artillery shell.

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And does it sometimes -- and shells as well?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is true for conventional shells which can be fired from tanks. Because the principal is that the shell is spinned by the interior part of the barrel and this is the same phenomenon as we can experience in the case of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And the mortar is stabilised by the fin at the back of the shell at one end of the shell?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The mortar?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The mortar shell is stabilised in flight by the fin, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We are just waiting for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously we can't speak about these two things at the same time. Because there is a difference between artillery using barrels, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Let us speak about mortar, mortar rounds. Are they stabilised in flight by the fin?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand your question. I just wanted to distinguish between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just let us deal with that question and then we can get to the distinction, that are mortar rounds stabilised in flight by the fin?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mortar shells are stabilised by the fins.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are mortar rounds in flight subsonic or supersonic or --

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here again, I have got to say that this depends. It can be both or either. Depending on the speed, depending on the charge when firing, and obviously the speed can change once the shell is on its trajectory. From an artillery table, you can -- you can see that quite easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Doctor, let us talk only about mortar rounds. Mortar rounds. Do they travel faster or slower than speed of sound?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do understand your question. But my answer is they can be either. And this depends on the charge in the firing stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Are you -- I heard earlier you referred to the depth that a tail-fin might go in asphalt as being outside of your area of expertise. Is the analysis of craters within your area of special training and knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VILMOS KOVACS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't. Crater analysis itself is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Dr. Kovacs, this concludes your testimony in this court. I thank you very much for having come to The Hague, having answered all the questions of both parties and the Bench and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then adjourn until a quarter past 11.00. I was informed, Ms. Pilipovic, that it might be possible to create a videotape with the B/C/S translation in a relatively short time. I don't know how much time you would have available to wait until the video would be ready, but do you have any arrangements that you have to leave at a certain time from The Hague, so that we can verify whether "relatively short" is quick enough?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I could get the audio tape this afternoon, it will mean a great deal, because it would mean that I could send it to Belgrade this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think this afternoon would be no problem. Would you prefer to have an audio tape rather than a videotape or both?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have both, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have only one question. Would it be possible for the expert to look at the tail-fin which is in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is one of the exhibits. I think under the supervision of the Registry, it could be inspected by your expert, but the remaining question is then, would that have any impact on the presence of Dr. Kovacs or is it just for future. For future.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only for the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you then please follow the instructions of the Registry, because it is the Registry who is finally responsible for the surveillance of all objects.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, is it appropriate for Mr. Philipps to set up his laptop to commence evidence immediately after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is what we more or less expected. That is also the reason why we continued a bit later. I have to apologise to the interpreters, but we will have a break now until a quarter pas 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, for your information, the audio tape will be ready within a couple of minutes after the -- after we adjourn. The videotape will be prepared so that also the charts are available to your expert because that might be important for him. But that takes a preparation time which is the same the evidence took. Well, let's just assume that we will continue until a quarter to 2.00, that would mean it would take approximately two and a half hours to prepare the videotape with the B/C/S language as well. Yes. Okay. It will then be put in your locker as soon as it is ready.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. What I would like to hear from our learned friends is whether they can confirm to me that the examination of Mr. Philipps will be resumed on Tuesday, the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is for sure? As sure as life can be?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed. General Abdul Razek is due to give evidence on Monday. Given the problems the Defence has with the arrangements of their expert. If the General does not finish on the Monday, then it seems to me appropriate that we accommodate the Defence by sticking to the timetable Richard Philipps to give evidence on the Tuesday and then return to General Abdul Razek, if needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that is confirmed. I take it that you at least agree with that Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before we return to the evidence of Mr. Philipps, in relation to Dr. Kovacs, do you require a formal tendering of his report or is the filing sufficient? I ask the question because his report does not bear a signature and in light of some problems we had with the report of Mr. Zecevic, we think it appropriate to clarify that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes Ms. Pilipovic, you heard the observation made by Mr. Ierace and you are aware of our decision in respect of Dr. Zecevic. I think the parties would agree that having gone through the report in some detail, there could be no -- at least I hardly could imagine that it would be in dispute that this is the report of -- which has been drafted and even been amended during the court session by the expert, Dr. Kovacs.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, during the cross-examination we received answers to some questions, however, the problem is that so far we have not received a copy of Mr. Kovacs' report in his mother tongue, the language that he wrote the report in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there -- well, neither have we seen it. The question is whether this is a document which plays any role. Is there an original available to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. With courtesy we indicated we would let the Defence have a copy. I think the copy is here. I thought it might have been handed over to him as well. The copy is here. I have seen that copy. However, the filing is not the Hungarian, for the purposes of this case, the filing is in the language used in the Tribunal, the English version. The Defence may if they want have a copy of the Hungarian document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can we -- we are in a procedural situation where the English version of the report has been filed, that is the report on which the Prosecution relies and on the basis of which questions have been put to the witness. If the Prosecution would provide the original report to the Defence, I think it is up to the Defence if they find any specific differences that, with the consent of the Prosecution, I think it could be introduced without being introduced by a witness. Would you agree with that? But only if there are good reasons to believe that the original report is a different one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is something that would be difficult to agree upon without the presence of the witness -- of the expert. There have been changes made to the original. It was important to the Prosecution to ensure that the English version, the version that could be tendered, was the one which he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp, of course, I am not referring to the changes made during the examination of the witness. But, for example, the conclusions would be totally different in the original version, then I can imagine that the Defence would like to introduce in one way or the other, even if it was just for the reliability of the expert. But let's do it this way: You provide the original to the Defence. If there would be any specific need for the Defence to introduce this report, we will have to find -- for specific reasons, then indicated, -- we would, of course, then have to consider that. If the Defence would say we have someone who speaks perfect Hungarian and says that the report is totally different from what the English translation says, then, of course there might be a different situation. We will cope with that as soon as the Defence indicates its desire to bring into evidence the original report for the reasons then to be indicated by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, so, Ms. Pilipovic, we will either hear from you or not hear from you. Then we could --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It will be on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I don't hear from you, I take it that there is no reason to deal with the matter any further. That means that we are now all ready to continue the examination-in-chief of Mr. Philipps. Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid all misunderstandings, so the filing at this moment is enough and it has the "P" number indicated because we have to register it in one way or another, but the filing is such is enough, no tendering necessary. utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.text: Mr. Philipps are you in a position to continue your examination utilizing your images that you started to show us last week?

utterances.text: Yes, I am

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am still looking for it and I can't find anything on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That, I have the same problem. Would it be possible -- have you opened the programme yet or not, Mr. Philipps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Philipps have some assistance in starting Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. his laptop. In commercials, it is always the little boy that puts in the plug but it seems not to be the situation here.

utterances.text: Any clue why it doesn't function? I am informed that we would need a break in order to -- does the laptop not function at all or is it just the programme that doesn't start?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]

utterances.text: Is this the second slide or the third slide in that sequence?
