utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, at the point that we left off last Friday, you said that you had marked, I think, 12 brigades on the chart. Firstly, were there in fact 12 brigades in the SRK during the indictment period?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of brigades in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps changed during the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please explain the detail of that change, according to the documents that you examine said.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Initially, two brigades which are shown on the top line were part of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, but then were passed to the Drina Corps on the 20th of November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, at that stage, could I stop you and invite you to continue the presentation at your own pace and in the manner that you have prepared.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide that I show you will see join as line from the corps headquarters to the corps support troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you now indicate the corps headquarters on the chart?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the corps headquarters and is connected by line to the corps support troops underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you now indicate on the chart a line following the right-hand edge of the chart to the bottom row or a row towards bottom?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, could you explain to us what you mean by the term, "corps support troops"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps support troops are a series of units which directly support the corps itself. That is, they are subordinated to the corps headquarters. These consist of units such as artillery, air defence, military police, logistics, medical, reconnaissance and engineers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In due course, during your presentation, will you return in more detail to those units?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A section of the presentation covers each of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue section shows those troops subordinated to individual brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the purposes of the transcript, perhaps as you move from one image to another, you might indicate, if you know it, the number of the image. Otherwise, simply indicate that you have progressed to the next image.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now, on the next image, I have highlighted the corps headquarters, so that I can talk specifically about the organisation of the corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before you move on, in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen, we see the number "3." Are each of the images sequentially numbered hereafter?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are sequentially numbered, however, some slides have multiple facets to them so that additional information is on each slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you change images could you please commence by identifying a number or other information that appears in the bottom right hand corner for the benefit of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The next slide is slide number 4. This is detail from the diagram on my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please indicate the relevant part of the chart with your pointer.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You indicate the top line within the corps headquarters block. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, we see on the screen a symbol. You told us earlier, that is on Friday, that you have employed NATO map symbols. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In this case, this is a linked to analysis symbol.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does a green human figure depict?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have used a green human figure where the information is confirmed that such an individual was in that position, that is, confirmed from multiple sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left of this we have General Major Tomislav Sipcic, who was the commander of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps during the dates or for part of the periods of the dates shown. There is then a dotted line to Colonel Stanislav Galic, who took over the Sarajevo Romanija Corps on the 9th of September 1992. The line is dotted to indicate that there was not specifically a handover from General Sipcic to Colonel Galic. But that General Sipcic, left the Sarajevo Romanija corps before Colonel Galic took over. We then see the date under then by then General Major Galic of the 10th of August 1994, which is the last date that the documents show he was in command of the corps. His position was then taken over by the next corps commander, Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just in relation to the date of the 10th of August, having regard to your answer, did you see a document saying that he definitely left that position on the 10th of August, or rather is it a matter of that being the last document you could find which referred to him as holding that position?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A combination of the two. Firstly, a document signed by the new corps commander, Dragomir Milosevic which by -- by which document I could see that General Galic ha relinquished command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the next line we can see the positions of chief of staff. The first being Colonel Dragan Marcetic who took over that position on the 29th of September 1992. He relinquished that position to a Colonel Dragomir Milosevic sometime between the 20th of June 1993 and the 6th of July, 1993 and then finally, Dragomir Milosevic on becoming the corps commander Cedo Sladoje became the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, coming back to the top line, you indicate, you depict rather, Dragomir Milosevic becoming the corps commander. Alongside his name on that line in brackets are the numbers 02. What is the significance of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number in brackets allows the index to be looked up under Dragomir Milosevic to relate to those documents which show him as being the corps commander. And also the number 2 indicates that it is the second time that Dragomir Milosevic appears on the diagram, as his name also appears under the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By the index to the documents, do you refer to the index which accompanied your report and contained I think approximately 60 pages of documentary references?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, also by way of explanation, alongside each reference in this image to dates, we see a little symbol which appears to be a reddish coloured square with something in it. Could you explain that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The symbols to the left of the lines underneath each name are in linked to analysis termed attributes. And these are simply symbols to allow the reader, when the chart is larger, to understand what each of those lines represents. So the small box which is very difficult to read on the small screen, actually show as calendar and this indicates that it is in fact a date. The block dot and the yellow dot simply differentiate between the position that an individual officer held and his rank of that particular time. And where an officer held more than one rank or was promoted over a period of time, both his ranks will be shown where they are known.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain to us the relationship between a corps commander and the chief of staff in terms of basic military corps structure.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of staff in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps is sometimes referred to as the deputy corps commander. In many respects, the chief of staff would be responsible for managing the operational staff within the corps headquarters. The corps commander would issue orders and directives which the chief of staff would put into action through working with the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you say "the corps commander would issue orders and directives," to what degree of detail would those orders and directives go as to the implementation of a strategy, if at all?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On some occasions, the orders might be written by the corps commander himself in detail. But on many occasions, the corps commander would merely explain his intention to the chief of staff and the chief of staff would engage the staff officers within the corps operational staff to put together the plan and to write the order. When this was finished, it would be put before the corps commander who was then able to sign it, having agreed that the staff work was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, perhaps this is obvious, but from the chart, but in any event to make it clearer, is the chief of staff, the immediate subordinate of the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide is slide number 5 and this shows in detail the operational staff of the corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to the area of the chart where now appears on the screen in slide number 5. You indicate the box to the immediate left within the corps command box. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This slide represents one of the four staff divisions within the corps headquarters and is split into several components. First of all, the top line shows one of the assistant corps commanders. The corps itself would have four assistant corps commanders responsible for different aspects of the staff. We can also see here that there is a different attribute or a different symbol used for some of the figures, and that is, a blue figure with a blank face. Where I have used a blue figure with a blank face, this indicates that the individual is unconfirmed in that position, and by that I mean that there was only one source of data that put that individual as being in that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many different sources of information did you rely upon in order to conclude that a particular person held a particular position?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were two reliable sources, then I considered it to be confirmed that an individual was in that position. Generally speaking, there were five or six or more pieces of information confirming an individual in a specific role or with a specific rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the purposes of this project as a whole did you presume that documents received from the Defence were reliable?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some respects, I presumed they were reliable. To qualify that, I should explain that they matched other data that was available, that they were consistent, and therefore, I took it that they were reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what of documents which were received from the Defence that could not be corroborated in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where there was a single document from the Defence which showed an individual in a particular position but which I could not confirm by another source, I have indicated the unit either by a dotted line or that the individual is shown in blue with a blank face, meaning that they are unconfirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, could I take you about to five minutes ago. I think you said that this box shows one assistant commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When one looks at the diagram, there appears on the face of it to be five assistant commander. So perhaps you could explain what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The horizontal arrows show the passage of command from one individual to another as they did on the corps commander slide. So the first assistant commander for organisation an mobilisation was Colonel Aleksa Krsmanovic. He hand over to all the Colonel Milan Malkovic and so on across the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do I take it, therefore, that you meant by that earlier observation that this shows, not so much one individual, but one post being the assistant commander for organisation and mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But it is one of the four posts of assistant corps commander that exist within the corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main and most important future on this chart is the box showing the operations and training. This staff division was responsible for putting together orders relating to operations and insuring that the troops had correct training. And here we see it is headed by a Colonel Cedo Sladoje. Again, we see a number 2 next to his name, showing that he appears on the entire chart twice. And we see that later on, of course, he became the chief of staff from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain to us what was involved in being an assistant commander -- being a chief of operations and training, what was the function of that person? You have mentioned training, but could you go into some more detail in relation to operations.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of operations was responsible for putting together the staff work, that is, the written orders and written instructions that follow the directives or orders of the corps command. So, Colonel Cedo Sladoje would be responsible for planning operations with the assistance of other staff officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other boxes on the side show an armoured operation staff and again showing two officers, one of whom took over from the previous officer. We can also see a signals and communication staff again responsible of relating to the corps commander the capability of his signal and communication equipment and insuring that communications and signals were functioning for any operation. Moving across to the right, we can see a series of sections, an office section, a computer section, an NBC defence or ABHO unit and electronic warfare staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you because I am trying to follow you and it might be difficult to come back to a certain point later. You said that in one of these boxes -- let me just find your words. An operation staff and again showing two officers, one of whom took over from the previous officer. So I would expect an arrow there, but apart from the top line, I don't see an arrows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On this diagram, I have not shown an arrow unless I know that one officer specifically handed over to another officer. In this case, for example, Lieutenant-Colonel Ratko Graorac was killed in action on the 8th of February 1993 and all the Colonel Ilija Petrovic does not appear in that position until the 25th of December 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and you would not use then the dotted arrow as you did before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could have used the dotted area but there should be another officer in between those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps, since we already have a break in your explanation, I might pick up on some other items that require amplification. Some of the boxes depicted with dotted lines and some with firm lines. What is the significance of that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where there is a dotted line, this shows that the existence of that formation is not fully confirmed, that is, I do not have two separate reliable sources to show the existence of such a staff. Where there is a full line, that is not dashed or dotted, this chose that I have data from two or more reliable sources indicating that such a staff exist said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Each of the -- or rather I should say, some of the boxed titles have capital letters underneath them. To given an example, "armoured operations" has underneath it the capital letters "OM" either "J" or "I". First of all, is it a J or I and what is the significance?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The abbreviation OMJ is from the B/C/S and I believe relates to an operational armoured unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were in the process of going through the small boxes which appear towards the centre of the screen in a different dotted line, boxes titled "office," "computer section" and so on. Could you explain the significance of the different dotted line, firstly.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Where the dotted line is quite faint this is because a document shows that such an organisation existed, but I have no confirmation that it should exist or that it does exist, nor have I found any personnel relating to that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this means, these are organisations that might fall within the order of battle of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, but I have no confirmed documents to show that they did in fact exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One of those boxes is titled "NBC defence." Could you explain that title?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: NBC defence, which stands for nuclear biological and chemical defence, is a direct translation I believe of ABHO, which is the B/C/S abbreviation or military abbreviation for nuclear biological and chemical defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you continue to go through the boxes where you left off?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next box on the right is air defence. This is not of course the unit of air defence, but it is the staff officers responsible for air defence for advising the corps commander on air defence and for insuring that appropriate air defence was available for any operation. In the bottom left of the diagram is the engineer staff. In the box is the commander of engineers and the date at which he took over or a date at which he was in that post. We then see two other boxes, reinforcement and personnel and an administration section. These again are unconfirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there any significance in the different type of dotted line for those two boxes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in this case that the dotted line for reinforcement and personnel is the same as that for office computer section and NBC defence. But the slight increase in size due to the computer has made the dotted line look slightly different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The final staff on this diagram is the artillery staff showing two officers, all the Colonel Radisav Cvetkovic and Colonel Tadija Manojlovic. Both of these officers appear to be in the artillery staff at the same time, although Radoslav Cvetkovic is not confirmed as the chief of artillery. The artillery staff were responsible for insuring that appropriate artillery staff was available to the corps commander for his operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, just by way of summary, in relation to the contents of the operations box, do I understand you to be saying that their primary function was to advise the Main Staff or the corps commander of the state of readiness for the various facilities under -- I am sorry -- the various facilities, according to their area of knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two aspects. One, to advise the corps commander, but also to ensure that such facilities were available. Perhaps a better description of the operations is that they respect the fighting arms of the Sarajevo Romanija Corp.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide, which is number 6, shows the morale staff organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to where that is on the chart, if you will.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 6 shows two officers, one taking over from the other. The first one being Colonel Ljubo Kosovac, and the second being Colonel Luka Dragicevic. These officers were corps commanders for morale legal and religious affairs. Here there may be a translation issue relating to the words "morale" as it is sometimes translation as moral, there being two words in English, but I believe in B/C/S and in French, only one word.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you explain the function of this unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The function of the staff for moral, legal and religious affairs was to inform the corps commander of the status of morale within the corps, but also to maintain that morale and ensure that it was at a high level. The organisation is divided into three parts and maybe more parts than three. Firstly, a section for political activities, a military club and a legal section. Again, all these three parts of this organisation are unconfirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you come across any information as to the nature of the function of the legal section?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Generally, in relation to the structure of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps are you able to comment on the degree to which, if at all, it follows the structure to a corps of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The structure and organisation of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps is similar to a corps within what was the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide is number 7 and shows the security staff section.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please briefly point to where it is located on the chart overall.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this staff section is headed by a corps assistant commander for intelligence and security, sometimes known as the chief of security, in this case, Colonel Marko Lugonja. I have very little information about this staff section, except for the fact that it is confirmed as existing by multiple documents. This staff section would be responsible for, not only intelligence on the enemy and the activities of the enemy which it would gain through the troops on the ground, but also for the security of the corps itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mentioned that a source of intelligence or resource was troops on the ground. If the SRK had available to it, sources of information on enemy territory, would that come through this unit or a different unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ideally all information relating to combat intelligence, that would be channelled through this organisation, whether they came from subordinate units or subordinate troops or from other sources or indeed from the Main Staff of the VR.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now explain the dark box which appears on the image?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The box itself rather like the others represents a security staff. This one is looking rather empty because there is very little information about what was actually contained within the security staff section. It is possible that it was very small or it may be that I simply have no information on that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide which is slide number 8, shows parts of the logistics staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the transcript you now indicate the relevant part of the chart which is towards the right of the corps command box.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This staff section represents the fourth of the staff sections within the corps headquarters. And again, is commanded by a corps assistant commander, this time for corps rear services. Throughout most of the period it was commanded, as shown on the right of the slide, by Colonel Aleksa Krsmanovic who commanded that staff section from the 20th of November 1992 until at least October 1993 and possibly longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that indicated by the dash which appears after the date October 1993, in other words, that it was at least until that date?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The last document I am able to find -- excuse me. The last document I have found showing Colonel Aleksa Krsmanovic as the corps assistant commander for corps rear services is dated October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Wherever else that symbol appears, does it have the same meaning?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The other boxes on the slide show, first of all, technical service, which was responsible for the technical assistance to the corps, that is, the repair of equipment, the servicing of equipment and instructions to the troops on how equipment should be maintained. There is a section for procurement and sale which is unconfirmed, a finance section or PMF, a veterinary service responsible for any animals used by the corps and finally an unconfirmed reinforcement section.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you explain the purpose of a reinforcement section.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I could only speculate which would be of little value.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 9 is a continuation of the logistics staff. At the top of the slide I have shown again the corps assistant commander as he was also in charge of this part of the staff. This staff is divided into two parts. The transport services responsible for the movement of supplies, materiel, that is, ammunition and war supplies, to the troops of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and the supply services who were responsible for obtaining and maintaining those supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On slide number 10, there is an additional staff division not normally found within the structure of the corps and that is the liaison section. Here there are four individuals named and then a separate section within liaison relating to air force liaison. First of all, on the left we have Colonel Komnen Zarkovic, then Captain, but later promoted, Milenko Indic. We have a Branko -- I beg your pardon. A Major Branko Milosevic who was liaison at the airfield, Butmir. And we have a first Captain Brane Luledzija, who was liaison with UNPROFOR. This is a separate staff section from the normal staff found within a corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 11 returns to the main diagram so that I can highlight two specific units. These two units are the Rogaticka Brigade and the 2nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is no need to show that on the chart since we have the chart on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I highlight these units both of which are brigades. They remained under the command of the corps headquarters until the 20th of November, 1992 when they were resubordinated to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just before you continue could you tell us, if you know, what is the -- what was the size of a brigade in the SK, in other words, how many members?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A brigade within the Sarajevo Romanija Corps could vary from a few hundred individuals up to the size of 5.000. And that is something I am able to cover later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In terms of the basic structure of the corps, you have told us something of the relationship between the chief of the Main Staff and the corps commander and the rest of the Main Staff and the corps commander. Is the brigade the next level down?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite correct, there is a direct contact between the corps commander and the brigade commander. The staff is merely facilitating that contact, but does not represent a step in the level of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, is the immediate superior to a brigade commander the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue with your explanation of this image number 12.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am showing each, the brigade commander at a particular time of these brigades were known, but it may not relate to the date when these brigades were under the command of General Galic. That is, brigade commander Rajko Kusic was in charge of that brigade in January 1993, but I have no reason to believe or no evidence that he was the commander of the brigade on the 20th of November, 1992. All the Colonel Milorad Krstic is shown as the brigade commander on the 13th of June 1992 and again he may or may not have been the brigade commander on the 20th of November 1992. The fact that is of value is that these corps -- sorry -- these brigades took no further part in the battle for Sarajevo as they were posted to the Drina Corps on that date. Slide number 13 returns to the main diagram and highlights the 1st Gradiska Light Infantry Brigade. Slide number 14 shows that this brigade was temporarily attached to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps during the Operation Lukavac 1993. So this brigade was temporarily under the command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, but only for that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was that operation, briefly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operation Lukavac 1993 was, I believe, was an attempt to close the corridor that was in use by the ABiH to and from Gorazde, that is, to seal off the communications and supply routes to the south of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is a date which appears in the box of the 15th of July 1993, followed by the hyphen symbol. What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That date is actually the date of the document that attaches the Gradiska Light Infantry Brigade to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. I do not have a date for when it was resubordinated to the 1st Krajina Corps and can only assume that it was at the conclusion of the Operation Lukavac 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide 15 returns to the main diagram and indicates the position of the headquarters of the Vogosca Operational Group and further shows the four brigades which formed part of the Vogosca Operational Group. These brigades were the Ilidza Brigade, the Ilijas Brigade, the Rajlovac Brigade, and the Vogosca Brigade. Slide number 16 shows details of the headquarters of the Vogosca Operational or Tactical Group. This group appears to have been formed, first of all, on the 15th of September, 1992, and was later reformed on the 19th of July, 1993. In its first incarnation, the group appears to be commanded by Colonel Vukota Vukotic and later in July 1993 was commanded by all the Colonel Dragan Josipovic. The details of the brigades under this group will be covered at later slides.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you learn anything of the apparent function of this operational or tactical group in relation to the four brigades?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The four brigades mentioned are all to the north and to the north-west of Sarajevo, on the opposite side from Lukavica, that is, from the corps forward headquarters. It seems that this operational group or tactical group was formed to have better control over the brigades on the opposite side of Sarajevo from the corps tactical -- sorry, corps forward headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to that answer, does it, therefore, follow that the operational group commander was in something of a superior role in relation to those four brigades, individually? In other words, they, in some sense, came between the brigades and the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be correct to assess that the corps commander commanded the officer in charge of the operational group, who himself commanded the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to Dragan Josipovic could you explain the reference to the date, having regard to your earlier explanation, does it mean that you located a document which indicated he held that position on the 9th of July 1993, and may well have done so both before and after that date?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. You can also see a question mark in the top left corner after the 15th of September, 1992. The reason for the question mark is that if the brigade -- I am sorry -- if the operational group was reformed on the 19th of July, 1993, one would have to assume that at some time it had been disbanded or removed in order for it to be reformed. And the reason for the question mark is it is unclear to me what date the Vogosca Operational or Tactical Group ceased to exist, whether it did cease to exist and exactly how or why it was reformed at a later date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just in relation to that, given that a document or more than one document referred to it being reformed on the 19th of July, 1993, it follows that another document referred to Dragan Josipovic being the operational group commander 10 days before the reformation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My assessment to that is, it is very normal to post a commander into a job before a unit exists or before an organisation exists so that he is able to oversee its formation or reformation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Finally, does the number 3 in brackets alongside his name indicate that he appears three times in the chart?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This is his third appearance in the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chart -- slide number 17 returns to the main diagram. And here on the left deals with the Igman Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before continuing, if you think you could do it in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. three or four minutes, the next slide, please proceed. If however, it would take more time, then I prefer to have the break now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it would take more than three or four minutes to go through the brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we get a lot of detailed information. Could you perhaps guide the witness in such a way that those names and dates that have no specific importance for the case, could be left out. We will read that if we don't -- if we would like to know these names, we can read them. Of course, on the other hand it might be that certain names are of specific importance. Would you guide the witness and ask for those specific names, for example, names that have been mentioned several times, for example in the liaison atmosphere that these are important to draw the attention to. The Chamber could not memorise them all. So we have to read them any how.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President, and the chart will now speak for itself. The reason behind the first few -- information was to show the process. I take the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, structure is also important, but not always names and dates. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With that in mind, Mr. Philipps, we now have on screen the Igman Infantry Brigade setting out the relevant holders of the senior positions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It seems that nothing there requires further explanation. Is that your view?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be worth just mentioning why there are various names for the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously there is the English the Igman Infantry Brigade and then the B/C/S, which I don't attempt to read. But also there is the abbreviation for the brigade IG PBR, that is the most commonly used terms for the documents. That is IG PBR is the most common terms used in the documents to refer to the Igman Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And on Friday you explained reference to the VP, that is the reference used within the Army of Republika Srpska which was unique to its unit, in this case the brigade is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you can go to the next image, number 19

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If consequence is always one of the worst things to experience. But do I see that you are here using the Cyrillic alphabet. Is there any specific reason -- I see a name under -- it is not clear on my screen but the top right-hand corner, first name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It looks -- no it is not Cyrillic. It is a "J" followed by an "I." It is not a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay, now it is clear to me. I have a very bad image on my screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please move to the next box.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just checked video evidence button. If you are using that button, you will find the computer evidence button is much clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I used that, as a matter of fact. What I see is that there are bright shades on the screen all the time behind block letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On my computer, I see the same. If I press the video evidence button, but if I press the computer evidence button, it is totally clear

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are totally right. I took the wrong one. I apologise for the inconvenience and the waste of time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, would you please point to the relevant part of the chart for the image that we see now?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In other words, we are now seeing what is under the box for the Igman Infantry Brigade is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The previous slide showed the headquarters and the remaining slides show the subordinating units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In this image for the first time we see a symbol indicating in this instance "mortars"; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that is symbol, as you understand it, used for NATO mapping purposes?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The symbol is simply a square or rectangular box with a dot in the middle representing artillery or mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The reference to Hadzici in the top two boxes is a reference to the shorthand name for the brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The brigade is sometimes called the Hadzici Brigade and the battalions were also sometimes called Hadzici Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it a standard part of military structure that brigade is comprised of battalions?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the size of a battalion in the SRK, according to the documents you have examined?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The size of a battalion within the corps, that is, subordinated to each of the brigades, could vary from an as little in one case as 56, up to as many in one case over 700. So the battalions varied enormously in size, depending on their role and the number of casualties that they had suffered.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The first box refers to two mortar platoons. What was the size of a platoon in the corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mortar platoons that were attached to battalions varied in size from 2 mortars up to as many at 8 mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the top left-hand corner of the first box alongside a red hyphen, appears the word and numbers "strength, 616." And then a date. Could you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A document supplied -- I am sorry. I am wrong there. Documents obtained from another source gave the strength of this first battalion in September 1995 as 616.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The unconfirmed platoon, which you describe as a reconnaissance platoon, has in brackets after it the word "Munja," what is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Munja perhaps one might call it nickname that was given the reconnaissance platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there anything else of significance in that slide?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is worth pointing out that each battalion consists of a number of infantry companies which are not shown on the diagram. So each battalion may have between two, up to as many seven infantry companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the size of a company?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A company again could vary from as little sometimes at 10 men up to as many a 100 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there any particular reason why you have not shown the companies?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not shown the companies because I have no specific documents or collection of documents that indicates the number of companies within the first battalion or the second battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please move to slide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one question. It is indicated after 82 millimetre mortar platoon, a "2" which indicates that it is mentioned for the second time, as far as persons are concerned, I have no difficulties in understanding. How would I have to understand the two here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here the two assists in finding the reference to the 82 millimetre mortar platoon for there are several 82 millimetre mortar platoons. This reference enables the ERN numbers to be located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is in order to distinguish it from other 82 millimetre mortar platoons. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please move to image 20.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Image 20 shows the artillery and supporting units attached to the Igman Brigade. It is clear that not all the units that are normally attached to a brigade are shown on this diagram. So it is likely that there are other units which I have not identified and I have, therefore, not shown that would be expected to appear in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the first box -- well, perhaps you could tell us a little more about the three types or sizes of artillery that are described.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the artillery attached to the Igman Brigade, I was shown three different types of artillery. The first is a 152 millimetre gun Howitzer. The second is a 105 millimetre M-56 Howitzer. And the third is a 76 millimetre or more correctly 76.2 millimetre ZIS gun which was also capable of being used as a Howitzer. The size of these units is not known. They are shown as being part of the artillery of the Igman Brigade through the supply of ammunition for those weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Above each artillery reference, do we see a NATO symbol for artillery?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If there is nothing else of significance in the slide, could you move to number 21.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 21 returns to the main chart and indicates the position of the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us on Friday that you have shown the brigades in the order in which they occupied the front line as one moved clockwise around Sarajevo. I take it the Igman Infantry Brigade was located in the area of Mount Igman. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Igman and Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it follow that the 2nd Sarajevo Light infantry Brigade was located directly to the north of the Igman Brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in this case the chart is slightly or could be considered to be out of order as the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade was really slightly to the other side of the Igman Brigade in the area of Vojkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down. The French booth is kindly asking this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise. I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The box on the chart for the 2nd Sarajevo Brigade appears lighter than the others. Is there any reason for that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade was a much smaller unit than many of the other brigades. Some of the brigades within the corps were only the size of battalions in a normal structure, and sometimes only the size of reinforced companies. The 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade is an example of one of the brigades that was really the size of a reinforced battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you please slow down your delivery a little. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This slide shows the headquarters of the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think that is self explanatory, unless there is anything of significance, perhaps you could move to the next image.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next image shows the infantry battalions that were subordinated to the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade. As an example of strength, we can see on the right-hand side the Trnovo Battalion when formed on the 21st of April, 1993, had a strength of only 56 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could now move to image number 24, unless there is something of consequence.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will note that there is no attached unit, artillery, logistics, or military police to the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade that we have just seen. This is either because it relied on some other logistic or military police support or perhaps that I have simply not located the documents indicating that such supporting troops existed. The next diagram returns to the main chart and then shows the position of the Ilidza Brigade. The Ilidza Brigade lay to the north of the Igman Brigade and so now the clockwise layout of brigades around Sarajevo beginnings correctly on the chart. This diagram shows the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are we now seeing image 25?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Image number 25. The only matter of note and interest is first of all, the strength of this brigade, which is given on 11th of April, 1993, as 3.000. So we can see this is a much larger brigade than the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand from the documents that it was located in the area of Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The next slide is slide number 26. This shows the infantry battalions attached to the Ilidza Brigade, each consisting of a number of infantry companies, but not identified by any documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 27 shows the supporting arms attached to the Ilidza Brigade, that is, 105 millimetre Howitzers, 128 millimetre Oganj, which is a 32-barreled rocket launcher, and an anti-aircraft defence unit consisting of 30 by 2 millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And again, the numbers in brackets, given your earlier evidence, do not refer to the number of Howitzers, is that the case?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Again the numbers in brackets refer to the references.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We see a different symbol on the right-hand side for the cannon. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The standard NATO symbol for an anti-aircraft gun is a half circle surrounded by the dot for "artillery."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where the numbers are known, are they indicated in the same fashion that is, 30 anti-aircraft weapons of 2 millimetre in calibre, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I should explain that. This is a 30 millimetre cannon which has two barrels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, I am intervening. Usually I would wait, but in order to find back the picture later, it is perhaps a bit difficult. You, as far as I understood you well. You are talking about Howitzers, when you talked about 105 millimetres. The number is not indicated. Is the number known?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't found the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know the number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where I have found the numbers in documents I have indicated it on the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next slide number 28, returns to the main diagram and shows the position of the Ilijas Brigade. Here again, the most interesting thing is the strength in February 1994 of 4.738 soldiers and officers. And here again without going into details on the names, we can see Dragan Josipovic appearing, who had previously appeared as the commander of the Vogosca Operational Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to him, I take it the hyphen after the 5th of March 1993 indicates that he held the position of brigade commander at least until that date. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And in relation to Bozidar Savic, we see that he was brigade commander until some time in 1994?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. He was no longer the brigade commander some time in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And we can take it that Dragan Josipovic was no longer commander of the brigade by some time in August 1993 at the latest, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We have seen from previous data that he probably became the commander of the Vogosca Operational Group in July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And do you mean by that it seems that at that point he relinquished the position of brigade commander of Ilijas?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the next slide, we see the first four battalions of the eight infantry battalions within the Ilijas Brigade. And here for the first time we have data on the number of companies, infantry companies, within the battalions. And also the number of mortars attached to each battalion and in addition, the strengths of each battalion at specific times.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We see on this image again different symbols. The rectangle with the cross, what does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rectangle with the cross is used to indicate infantry and the rectangle, which isn't very clear, but the rectangular the circle and the cross running through it represents a reconnaissance unit. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is there anything else of significance in that image?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We then have the remaining four of the eight infantry battalions within the Ilijas Brigade. Again, showing infantry company numbers where known, and also attached mortars where known. And we have seen that within the brigade, strengths of battalions vary enormously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 32 -- excuse me. Slide number 32 shows the supporting arms of the Ilijas Brigade, specifically an armoured mechanised company, probably consisting of mechanised infantry combat vehicles. And interestingly, a sniper squad with a strength of six, attached directly to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I draw your attention to the artillery -- first of all, the mixed artillery divizija, in which you identify the battalion commander and then in a separate box underneath it, artillery. Could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The artillery for the Ilijas Brigade seems to be divided into two parts. And I have used the word "divizija," which is actually a B/C/S word. Probably the best translation might be "battalion." But a divizija is a special word a specific word, again one of those words that is not easy to translate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The first item in the artillery box reads 122 millimetre M-38 and then times one. Can you explain the times one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case the by one actually refers to the number of 122 millimetre pieces. I have included it because it is normally very unusual to see one artillery piece on its own. The reasons for this are that one artillery piece, especially of a different calibre, would then require a separate artillery supply, separate artillery ammunition supply just for that one piece. Normally you would expect to find a multiple number. In this case it may be that the 122 millimetre M-38 is able to fire the same ammunition as the 122 millimetre D-30.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. Returning briefly to the meaning of the word divizija, having regard to your answer, it seems it does not mean division. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sometimes is translated as division. But that could cause confusion, as that is a very large artillery organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Finally in relation to that page, in the to right-hand corner you have Vasko's Platoon with its own VP number. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you comment at all on the fact that it had its own VP number, what, if anything, does that tell you as to whether Vasko and his men were a part of the SRK or no?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VP number which stands for "vojna post" [phoen], army post, for the Ilijas Brigade is 7491. Each of the units subordinated to the Ilijas Brigade uses that four-figure designation, followed by its own two-digit number. The fact that any of these units, including Vasko's Platoon have a VP number 7491, shows them to be part of the organisation of the Ilijas Brigade and in addition, the number 20 indicates it to be a separate unit of the Ilijas Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given the box is not a dotted line, do I take it that you found more than one source for that information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There are several, several documents referring to that platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember anything as to the nature of any of those documents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to look them up on the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Sorry, what are the 40 millimetre Bofors guns.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the anti-aircraft defence box, there are marked 40 millimetre Bofors guns. This is an anti-aircraft gun which I believe is in a pair or three guns mounted on a fixed base, that is, it is not on the back of a truck, but it can be towed. It is normally used for anti-aircraft and has a range of about 4 kilometres into the air but of course is very accurate when fired against the ground target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only other box of notes is the mixed antitank divizija or battalion, but I have no informations to what weapons were held in that organisation. The next slide is number 33 and shows the other supporting arms for the Ilijas Brigade. These are not part of the fighting units of the brigade but assist the brigade in its normal daily activity, such as supply or medical services or military discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue. For the record, this is image number 33, I think. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one question, ABHO, what stands that for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, we have a platoon ABHO is the B/C/S abbreviation of a military abbreviation NB, which is nuclear, biological and chemical defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mentioned that before. I apologise. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slide number 34 returns to the main diagram and shows the Rajlovac Brigade. Slide number 35 shows the headquarters of the Rajlovac Brigade

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I can stop you there for a moment. Did the territory controlled by that brigade, as you understood it, control the area of the Rajlovac?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. This brigade is similar to the 2nd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade and it is much smaller than some of the other brigades and really only consists of a battalion-sized unit. Slide number 36 shows the units that form part of the Rajlovac Brigade, that is, one infantry battalion and some attached artillery. Neither of these units nor the commanders are confirmed, that is, there is only one document that relates to these individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could point to the area of the chart which appears on that image.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 37 returns to the main chart and shows the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And again, did its area include the Serbian Army side closest to Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Slide number 38 shows the headquarters of the Vogosca Light Infantry Brigade. Slide number 39 shows the infantry and also tank unit that formed part of the Vogosca Brigade. And again, we see that this is a relatively small brigade, consisting really of a reinforced battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We also see in that image the symbol for tanks.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. A simple rectangle with a track shape in the centre. The tank shown is a T-55 tank, which is of Russian design, with 100 millimetre tank gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, if you know it, in a typical tank platoon, how many tanks there were?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually have no data for this specific tank platoon, but one would expect at least three tanks and possibly four tanks in a tank platoon. The next slide shows -- which is slide number 40 -- shows the brigade supporting arms for the Vogosca Brigade. Firstly, it shows the light anti-aircraft artillery unit consisting of two sections. One with 20 millimetre anti-aircraft guns and the second with 40 millimetre anti-aircraft guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What do the initials "PAT" stand for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a B/C/S abbreviation for anti-aircraft, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide, number 41, shows the attached artillery to the Vogosca Brigade. Again consisting of 122 millimetre gun Howitzers, 76 millimetre guns, a Plamen section, and Plamen is the B/C/S name for a 32-barreled 128 millimetre rocket launcher, but with a considerably less range than the one Oganj that was mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that multiple rocket launcher or a single rocket launcher?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a multiple rocket launcher. The next section shows the 128 millimetre Oganj and again this is a multiple rocket launcher, but with a longer range just over 20 kilometres. And finally, almost finally, we have a mixed Howitzer platoon with unidentified weapons. And finally on the right, not found to be within a unit, that is, attached to an unidentified unit of the artillery a T-12 antitank gun or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to that image, one of the boxes has some dates, that is, the 128 millimetre Oganj section. The other boxes do not. Could you assist us as to whether that means that the information you discovered was not only unconfirmed, as indicated by the dotted line, but does it also mean that you were unable to date the information?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It means I was unable to date it, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mean precisely that's correct or precisely you could not date it with precision?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We may have been able to work out a range of dates which the documents fell within, but it may be that the document itself did not have a specific date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one question in that respect. I see dotted lines are not always the same, especially vertical ones, the first and the fifth are different from the others. Is this just because it is very difficult to make them all the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it to be a software problem where one opposes a dotted line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there is no specific meaning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just coming back to my earlier questions, does that mean, for example, even in relation to the one source of information, in respect of the first box, that is 122 millimetre section, commander being Dragan Janjic, there is no information as to whether that was within the indictment period or not?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check the reference. But I believe I would not have included it on the diagram if it were outside the indictment period for this organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slide number 42 shows the 2 mortar battalion attached to the Vogosca brigade. The full structure of the battalions is not shown and only 120 millimetre mortar battery has been identified as part of the 1st Mortar Battalion. One would expect to see several other mortar batteries forming part of this mortar battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us something of the size of a mortar battalion and a mortar battery. Earlier you gave us some information on mortar platoons.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mortar battery may consist of a series of mortar platoons, each of which may have four mortars. So a battery in some circumstances, can consider to be 8 pieces and with two batteries in a mortar battalion, a battalion might be considered to consist of 16 or of course it may have 3 batteries, in which case it would consist of 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next slide, number 43, returns to the main diagram and the arrow on the diagram indicates the formation of a new organisation, the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade. This organisation appears to have been formed from the headquarters, first of all of the Vogosca Brigade. And the units that were within the Rajlovac Brigade, the Vogosca Brigade and the Kosevo Brigade. Slide number 44 shows the headquarters of the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just before we continue with that, did that occur somewhere between October 1993 and March 1994, that is, that the Vogosca Brigade was incorporated into the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And had the Rajlovac Light Infantry Brigade been move and in the process down sized in January 1994, that is incorporated?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The Rajlovac Brigade as already been stated, was a smaller organisation. It was only really a battalion-sized organisation. That became part of -- that is one of the battalions within the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And was the Kosevo Light Infantry Brigade moved and downsized at the same time as the Rajlovac Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Is that information contained on the chart?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all on the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I ask you, we will stop at a quarter to 2.00. And I would need just a couple of minutes three, four, five, minutes, perhaps partly in closed session, to deal with a few procedural matters. Would you find a suitable moment to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is something that I wish to raise in closed session as well. I wonder if we can go into the closed session and deal with these matters

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the presence of the matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the other matters it would not be convenient to do it in the presence of the witness. So we stop now at chart 45 and we turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now. I would like to ask the Defence more specifically to prepare for some questions in respect of what the Chamber would have to expect from the Defence case. We have to plan well in advance a lot of things, that means, whether during the recess we expect anything from the parties or not or that we wait until after the recess and then make new schedules. But one of the elements in it would also be how many witnesses, approximately, I am not asking for a final figure, we could expect and how much time in view of the Defence the examination of these witnesses approximately would take, and how to measure that time needed to examine these witnesses. We will discuss this perhaps in relation with the other questions, the questions about if the Defence would intend to file a motion to dismiss at what date it should be done, when an answer should be -- when the Prosecution should respond. So would you please prepare for, even if it would be a very short exchange of views, on these matters and give us at least some impression of what we can expect from the parties. And then certainly we will give you an impression of what we expect from you. Then we will adjourn, if there is nothing else on the agenda, for a bit longer period than usual, until next Monday, 9.00 same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th, day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
